newsitem.title: USA: PageNet shares rise on VoiceNow outlook.
newsitem.headline: PageNet shares rise on VoiceNow outlook.

text.p: Shares of Paging Network Inc climbed steadily on Thursday after the company made bullish comments to analysts about its VoiceNow paging product.
PageNet said it expected to launch the voice messaging service in the first quarter of 1997 and expand the VoiceNow system by about one million units a year, analysts said.
Shares of the Dallas-based company jumped 1-5/8 to 17-1/2 in afternoon trading.
Christopher Larsen, an analyst at NatWest Securities, said he was impressed by the upbeat outlook offered by the company's management during a conference call Thursday.
"They were so bullish about the VoiceNow product," he said, citing a company survey that estimated the potential market of VoiceNow customers was 20 million subscribers.
"That would mean a million new VoiceNow units a year, which is just huge," Larsen said.
VoiceNow is a portable voice mail machine that carries messages over PageNet's narrowband personal communications services licenses.

Suzanne Stein, an analyst at Goldman Sachs, said the company's strong third-quarter earnings posted Thursday morning -- coupled with management's confidence in a first-quarter launch of VoiceNow -- helped the stock recover from a slight decline on Wednesday.
"Their margins are excellent, and I think it just shows they are the low-cost provider," she said.
In another sign that product tests are going well, Stein said, the company has scheduled a December 9 analysts' meeting in Dallas to outline the VoiceNow marketing strategy.

"I think it is very important to them to have a good launch," she said. "Their plans for VoiceNow are clearly very big. It is voice mail you can take with you. This device does have mass market potential."
PageNet posted third-quarter net loss of $0.21 per share compared with a loss of $0.10 per share in the year-earlier quarter. Operating cash flow rose 24.9 percent to $65 million from $54 million.
The company said domestic pagers in use rose to 8.4 million, a 36.8 percent increase from the 1995 period.
